(a) **Chiral vs Achiral:**
A **chiral molecule** is non-superimposable on its mirror image (lacks a plane or center of symmetry) and exhibits optical activity. An **achiral molecule** is superimposable on its mirror image and possesses a plane or center of symmetry.

(b) **$	ext{E}$ or $	ext{Z}$ Configuration:**
(i) $	ext{H}_3	ext{C}-	ext{CH}=	ext{CH}-	ext{CH}_3$ (assuming trans-2-butene format): **E**
(ii) $	ext{H}-	ext{C}(	ext{CH}_3)=	ext{C}(	ext{Br})-	ext{Cl}$: **Z** (Higher priority groups on same side)
(iii) Symmetrical or single-substituted alkene lacks geometric isomerism / not applicable.
(iv) $	ext{H}_3	ext{C}-	ext{C}(	ext{H})=	ext{C}(	ext{Cl})(	ext{Br})$: Depends on specific stereocenter layout; typically designated by Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priorities.

(c) **Enantiomers vs Diastereomers:**
* **Enantiomers:** Non-superimposable mirror images of each other. They have identical physical and chemical properties except the rotation of plane-polarized light.
* **Diastereomers:** Stereoisomers that are *not* mirror images of each other. They have different physical and chemical properties.
* *Example:* D-glucose and D-galactose are diastereomers (epimers).

(d) **$	ext{R}$ or $	ext{S}$ Configuration:**
(i) Assign CIP priorities to groups attached to chiral carbon and trace $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3$. If lowest priority ($	ext{H}$) is vertical, clockwise = $	ext{R}$, counter-clockwise = $	ext{S}$. (Typically determined as per standard Fischer projection rules).
(ii) Apply the same priority sequence ($-	ext{Br} > -	ext{CH}_3 > -	ext{H}$).
proTip: For E/Z configuration, always apply the Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) priority rules to the two substituents on each carbon of the double bond.
